draft.title: Periodic table trends
card: A period is a row of the periodic table. A group is a column. Three properties change in a regular way along a period and down a group.
Across a period
Atomic radius falls. First ionisation energy (the energy to remove one electron from an atom) and electronegativity (how strongly an atom attracts shared electrons) both rise.
Down a group
Atomic radius rises. First ionisation energy and electronegativity both fall.
Why

Across a period, the nuclear charge grows while electrons are added to the same energy level, so the outer electrons are pulled in more strongly. Down a group, outer electrons sit in higher energy levels, further from the nucleus and held more weakly.
draft.remember: Across a period, the pull on outer electrons grows. Down a group, it weakens.

a.q: Which change occurs from left to right across a period?
opts: First ionisation energy rises and atomic radius falls
First ionisation energy falls and atomic radius rises
Both first ionisation energy and atomic radius rise
Both first ionisation energy and atomic radius fall
a.why: Across a period, outer electrons are pulled in more strongly, so the atom gets smaller and more energy is needed to remove an electron. The second option describes the trend down a group instead.
a.clue: Think about how strongly the nucleus pulls on the outer electrons.

b.q: Rubidium is below potassium in Group 1. Compared with potassium, rubidium atoms have which properties?
opts: A larger radius and a lower first ionisation energy
A larger radius and a higher first ionisation energy
A smaller radius and a lower first ionisation energy
A smaller radius and a higher first ionisation energy
b.why: Down a group, outer electrons are in a higher energy level, further from the nucleus. The atom is larger and the outer electron is easier to remove. A higher ionisation energy is the trend across a period, not down a group.
b.clue: Moving down a group, are the outer electrons closer to or further from the nucleus?

a.best: First ionisation energy rises and atomic radius falls

b.best: A larger radius and a lower first ionisation energy

problems.detail: Why (a) refers to 'the second option', but the options are shown in a random order, so a student may see a different option in second place. The why should name the option's content (first ionisation energy falls and atomic radius rises) rather than its position.

check.summary: The facts and both answers are correct. The only problem is that why (a) points to 'the second option', which will be wrong once the options are shuffled, so it should name the option's wording instead.
